chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Misbah al-Mazni, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
The Takbirs of the prayer are ninety-five Takbirs in the day and night, including the Takbir of the Qunut.
ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs are recited in the five daily prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (AS) in *Al-Khisal* quantifies the ritual glorification of God within the five daily prayers, establishing a specific count of ninety-five Takbirs that underscores the centrality of divine praise in Shia devotional practice. By explicitly including the Takbir of Qunut, the tradition highlights the continuity between the formal pillars of prayer and the supplementary supplications, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on the spiritual weight of each utterance. This count serves as a tangible metric for worshippers to deepen their mindfulness (khushu) throughout the daily cycle of worship.
